groups.name: Web & App Engineering
groups.summary: Sites and web applications, from structure and interface through to a live, maintained service.

cards.name: HTML
cards.summary: Semantic document structure for accessible, crawlable web interfaces.
cards.what: I write clear, semantic HTML so pages are readable, accessible, and straightforward to maintain — including multi-page sites and single-page application shells.

cards.name: CSS
cards.summary: Layout, typography and responsive styling without a heavy framework.
cards.what: I style interfaces with plain CSS: compact spacing, clear hierarchy, and layouts that hold up on phones, tablets and desktops without pulling in a UI kit.

cards.name: JavaScript
cards.summary: Browser and server JavaScript for interactive interfaces and tooling.
cards.what: I use JavaScript directly in the browser and on the server for forms, search, real-time updates and small applications — without a required frontend framework.

cards.name: TypeScript
cards.summary: TypeScript for typed JavaScript in web applications and supporting tools.
cards.what: I use TypeScript when a web application or supporting tool benefits from typed JavaScript: clearer interfaces, safer refactors, and a compile step that still ships ordinary JavaScript to the browser or to Node.js.

cards.name: Testing & QA
cards.summary: Practical testing and quality checks for web applications and sites: test plans, regression checks, and catching breaks before a release.
cards.what: I write and run practical tests around the parts of a site or application that actually change: forms, critical paths, and regressions after a release or migration. The work stays proportionate to the size of the job, with notes your team can repeat.

cards.name: Apps Script
cards.summary: Google Apps Script automation for Google Sheets, Gmail, Drive, triggers, and Workspace tools.
cards.what: I write Google Apps Script to automate Sheets, Gmail, Drive and other Workspace tools, including triggers and the surrounding workflow work.

cards.name: Google Developer
cards.summary: Google Developer tools including Search Console, Tag Manager, Analytics, Workspace APIs and the web developer platform.
cards.what: I use Google Search Console, Google Tag Manager, GA4, AdSense, Apps Script and Google Workspace Developer APIs when a site or workspace needs search visibility, measurement, advertising or automation on Google's platform.

cards.name: Node.js
cards.summary: JavaScript on the server for web apps, APIs and local tooling.
cards.what: I build web services and command-line tools on Node.js, including zero-dependency apps that stay on the standard library where that is practical.

cards.name: Responsive UI and UX
cards.summary: Interfaces that stay usable across phone, tablet and desktop.
cards.what: I design and implement interfaces with compact controls, clear focus states and layouts that work at small sizes first, then scale up cleanly.

cards.name: Accessibility
cards.summary: Accessibility work for websites and web apps: semantic structure, keyboard use, labels, contrast and practical checks against common barriers.
cards.what: I improve the accessibility of websites and web applications with semantic HTML, usable keyboard paths, form labels, and contrast that holds up in light and dark themes. I check the pages people actually use and leave notes so the standard can be kept after the engagement.

cards.name: Embedding
cards.summary: Iframe embeds, map embeds, widget integration and third-party content embedding in web pages.
cards.what: I embed maps, widgets and other outside content in pages using sandboxed iframes, with responsive sizing and careful limits so third-party content stays contained and does not take over the page.

cards.name: Zero-dependency web apps
cards.summary: Self-contained applications that do not require a heavy package tree.
cards.what: I ship self-hosted web apps that run with little or no third-party runtime, so the stack stays understandable, portable and under your control.

cards.name: Single-page and multi-site architecture
cards.summary: Information architecture for one site, or a set of sites that share patterns.
cards.what: I plan page structure, routing and shared chrome for a single application or a group of related sites, so navigation and content stay consistent as the work grows.

cards.name: Website Migrations & Speed Optimisation
cards.summary: Website migrations and speed optimisation: moving a site cleanly and tightening the pages that people actually load.
cards.what: I migrate websites from one host or stack to another with a written cutover plan, and I tighten page weight, caching and image use so the pages people load are quicker without changing the meaning of the site.

cards.name: SEO
cards.summary: Search engine optimisation for public websites: titles, metadata, structure and Search Console.
cards.what: I set up the on-site foundations of search engine optimisation: unique titles and descriptions, clear headings, canonical URLs, a sitemap, and Google Search Console where a site needs to be found.

cards.name: Digital Marketing
cards.summary: Practical digital marketing for public sites: measurement, search, and on-site conversion paths.
cards.what: I support digital marketing work on the sites I build: measurement through Google Tag Manager and GA4, search foundations, and clear conversion paths such as hire and contact pages.

cards.name: WordPress
cards.summary: Self-hosted WordPress sites, themes, and plugin work.
cards.what: I set up and look after self-hosted WordPress sites: clear structure, themes and plugins, and the routine work that keeps a site running.

cards.name: Visual Studio
cards.summary: Building and debugging software with Visual Studio.
cards.what: I use Visual Studio to write, build and debug software, including Windows-focused work, with a clear project structure and a maintainable toolchain.

cards.name: GitHub
cards.summary: Public source control, issues and releases on GitHub.
cards.what: I use GitHub for public source control, issues and releases. Private repositories are not listed or linked on this site.

groups.name: Backend & Data
groups.summary: Services, storage, sign-in and the everyday data work that keeps a product running.

cards.name: Python
cards.summary: Python for scripting, automation, data work and backend services.
cards.what: I use Python for scripting, automation, data work and backend services, including the supporting tools around packaging, files and routine operational tasks.

cards.name: Java
cards.summary: Java for application work and supporting tools alongside Python and JavaScript.
cards.what: I use Java for application work and supporting tools when a project already lives on the JVM or is a better fit than Python or JavaScript for that piece of work.

cards.name: Node.js standard library
cards.summary: HTTP, file and process work using the Node.js standard library.
cards.what: Where it is practical, I keep server code on the Node.js standard library — HTTP services, file I/O and processes — so deployments stay small and easy to reason about.

cards.name: SQLite
cards.summary: Embedded SQL storage for applications that should stay self-hosted.
cards.what: I use SQLite for application data when a self-hosted, file-based database is the right fit: simple backups, clear schema, and no separate database server to operate.

cards.name: PostgreSQL
cards.summary: PostgreSQL for application data: schema, queries, backups and routine operation of the database.
cards.what: I use PostgreSQL for application data when a project needs a relational database: schema and queries, access, backups and the routine operation that keeps the database healthy beside the application it serves.

cards.name: MySQL / MariaDB
cards.summary: MySQL and MariaDB for application data, including schema, queries, backups and day-to-day operation.
cards.what: I work with MySQL and MariaDB for application data: schema and queries, access, backups and day-to-day operation, including sites and applications that already run on those engines.

cards.name: JSON
cards.summary: JSON for APIs, configuration, data interchange and structured records.
cards.what: I use JSON throughout API work, configuration and data interchange: request and response bodies, structured records, and the documents that scripts and web services pass between each other.

cards.name: CRM
cards.summary: Customer and enquiry records, structured follow-up, and integrations around a CRM workflow.
cards.what: I set up and integrate CRM workflows for enquiries and customer records: structured intake, follow-up, and the surrounding email or webhook connections a small organisation actually uses.

cards.name: Authentication
cards.summary: Sign-in, accounts and credential handling for web applications.
cards.what: I implement sign-in and account flows with careful handling of credentials, recovery and access control, suited to the scale of the application.

cards.name: Session security
cards.summary: Session cookies, expiry and protection against common session attacks.
cards.what: I set up session handling with secure cookies, sensible expiry and defences against session fixation and cross-site request issues.

cards.name: Automated backups
cards.summary: Scheduled copies of application data and configuration.
cards.what: I put automated backups in place for databases, files and configuration, with retention that can actually be restored from.

cards.name: CSV and PDF generation
cards.summary: Export of reports and records as CSV or PDF files.
cards.what: I generate CSV and PDF output from application data for records, invoices and operational reports, without a bulky reporting suite.

cards.name: Data Scraping & Web Automation
cards.summary: Authorised data scraping and web automation for repeatable collection, checks and operational scripts.
cards.what: I write authorised data collection and web automation for work I have been asked to do: repeatable scripts that gather, check and file information, with clear limits so the automation stays maintainable and respectful of the systems it touches.

cards.name: Ollama
cards.summary: Running and managing local AI models.
cards.what: I run and manage local AI models with Ollama: installing models, keeping them up to date, and wiring them into local tooling when a self-hosted setup is the right fit.

groups.name: Infrastructure & Self-Hosting
groups.summary: Servers, DNS, certificates, mail and the operations work that keeps systems online.

cards.name: Linux servers
cards.summary: Provisioning, hardening and day-to-day operation of Linux hosts.
cards.what: I set up and operate Linux servers for web applications and services: users, firewalls, process management, and the routine work that keeps a host healthy.

cards.name: Debian
cards.summary: Debian servers: install, hardening and day-to-day operations.
cards.what: I install, harden and operate Debian servers for web applications and services, including updates, users and the routine work that keeps a host healthy.

cards.name: Ubuntu
cards.summary: Ubuntu servers: install, updates and day-to-day operations on Ubuntu Linux.
cards.what: I install, update and operate Ubuntu servers for web applications and services, including packages, users and the routine work that keeps a host healthy.

cards.name: Docker
cards.summary: Container images, Compose files and local Docker workflows.
cards.what: I build and run container images and Compose files for local and server workflows, so services start the same way from one host to the next.

cards.name: cPanel
cards.summary: cPanel and WHM for hosting accounts, email, DNS and routine server administration.
cards.what: I work with cPanel and WHM to administer hosting accounts, email, DNS and the routine server tasks a small organisation needs, including backups and access for the people who use the accounts.

cards.name: VMware
cards.summary: ESXi, vSphere, virtual machines, hypervisor setup, and host administration.
cards.what: I set up and administer VMware hosts and virtual machines: ESXi and vSphere, hypervisor setup, and the day-to-day work of keeping guests running.

cards.name: Windows servers
cards.summary: Windows hosts for business applications, file services and local networks.
cards.what: I work with Windows servers in small business settings — applications, file services and the surrounding network — alongside Linux where both are in use.

cards.name: Windows desktop
cards.summary: Windows desktop setup, administration, troubleshooting and tooling.
cards.what: I set up and look after Windows desktop systems: installation, administration, troubleshooting and the everyday tooling that keeps workstations usable in a small business or workshop setting.

cards.name: Computer Builds
cards.summary: Specifying and assembling desktop and workstation builds for development and small business use.
cards.what: I specify and assemble desktop and workstation builds for development and small-business use, then install the operating system and the baseline software needed to put the machine to work.

cards.name: Computer Repairs
cards.summary: Diagnosis and repair of workstations and desktops, including hardware faults and operating system recovery.
cards.what: I diagnose and repair workstations and desktops: failing drives, memory, power and operating system recovery, with the aim of restoring a machine people can actually work on.

cards.name: Business IT
cards.summary: Day-to-day small business IT in Australia: workstations, email, domains, backups and support.
cards.what: I look after the practical IT a small organisation in Australia needs: workstations, business email, domains, backups and routine support, with a written scope and systems that can be maintained afterwards.

cards.name: Xero
cards.summary: Xero setup and supporting integrations for small-business bookkeeping and invoicing in Australia.
cards.what: I help small organisations in Australia get Xero in place and connected to the surrounding tools they already use, including users, invoicing workflows and the integrations a bookkeeping routine depends on.

cards.name: Quoting & Invoicing
cards.summary: Written quotes, invoices and payment terms for professional work, including Xero-based invoicing where that is the bookkeeping tool.
cards.what: I set up a clear path from a written quote to an invoice and recorded payment, including payment terms a small organisation can actually follow. Where Xero is the bookkeeping tool I use it for invoices and the surrounding workflow; the same discipline applies if invoices are issued another way.

cards.name: Microsoft 365
cards.summary: Microsoft 365 setup and support for mail, files and everyday business productivity in Australia.
cards.what: I set up and support Microsoft 365 for small organisations: mailboxes, domains, file libraries and the everyday productivity tools a team actually uses, with a clean cutover when moving from another mail host.

cards.name: Google Workspace
cards.summary: Google Workspace for business email, calendars, Drive and Workspace admin in Australia.
cards.what: I set up and administer Google Workspace for organisations that want business email, calendars and Drive on their own domain, including DNS and mail authentication for a clean cutover.

cards.name: Windows Automation
cards.summary: PowerShell scripting, scheduled tasks, and workstation automation.
cards.what: I write PowerShell scripts, scheduled tasks and workstation automation so routine Windows work runs on its own, with a clear, maintainable set of tasks rather than one-off manual steps.

cards.name: PowerShell
cards.summary: PowerShell scripting for Windows automation and administration.
cards.what: I write PowerShell scripts for Windows administration and automation: repeatable tasks, scheduled jobs and clear, maintainable scripts.

cards.name: Automation
cards.summary: Workflow automation, scheduled tasks, scripting, API pipelines, and repeatable operations.
cards.what: I design and build automation for repeatable operations: scheduled tasks, scripts, API pipelines and workflows that cut down routine manual work.

cards.name: DNS
cards.summary: Domain registration, nameservers, DNS records, DNSSEC, renewal and WHOIS, and mail-related DNS including SPF, DKIM and DMARC.
cards.what: I plan and maintain DNS and domain management for websites and mail: registration, transfers, nameservers, renewal and WHOIS, DNSSEC, and A, AAAA, CNAME, MX and TXT records including SPF, DKIM and DMARC, with changes made carefully.

cards.name: Networking Fundamentals
cards.summary: IPv4, IPv6, subnetting, routing and core networking concepts used in day-to-day infrastructure work.
cards.what: I work with IPv4 and IPv6 addressing, CIDR subnetting, VLANs, routing and firewalling, and I troubleshoot network issues when services need a clear path to the internet or to each other.

cards.name: VPN
cards.summary: Virtual private networks for secure remote access to business systems and internal services.
cards.what: I set up and support virtual private networks so people can reach business systems and internal services securely from outside the office, with access limited to the hosts and users who need it.

cards.name: TLS and ACME
cards.summary: Certificates and HTTPS for public sites and services.
cards.what: I put HTTPS in place with automatically renewed certificates, and keep certificate and redirect behaviour correct as domains change.

cards.name: Encryption & PGP
cards.summary: Practical encryption for mail, files and hosts, including OpenPGP where a team already uses it, alongside HTTPS already covered under TLS.
cards.what: I help teams use encryption in the places it actually protects them: OpenPGP for mail and files where that is already part of the workflow, and disk or volume encryption on hosts I operate. I do not publish a personal OpenPGP fingerprint on this site. Certificate and HTTPS work is covered on the TLS and ACME card.

cards.name: Email Deliverability
cards.summary: Email deliverability with SPF, DKIM and DMARC so business mail is authenticated and more likely to arrive.
cards.what: I improve email deliverability by setting SPF, DKIM and DMARC correctly on a domain, checking alignment, and tracing why messages bounce or land in junk, so business mail is authenticated and more likely to arrive.

cards.name: SMTP, DKIM and IMAP mail
cards.summary: Business email: self-hosted or managed, with correct DNS and authentication.
cards.what: I set up business email on a domain — self-hosted or managed — with SPF, DKIM and DMARC in place, and help with mailbox migrations.

cards.name: Reverse proxies
cards.summary: Front doors for web apps: TLS termination, routing and isolation.
cards.what: I place reverse proxies in front of applications for TLS, host routing and a single public entry point, so services stay isolated on the private side.

cards.name: Uptime monitoring
cards.summary: Checks and alerts when a site or service stops responding.
cards.what: I set up uptime and health checks so outages are noticed quickly, with alerts that go to the people who can act on them.

cards.name: Cybersecurity & Server Hardening
cards.summary: Cybersecurity and server hardening for Linux and Windows hosts: access, updates, firewalls and baseline configuration.
cards.what: I harden Linux and Windows servers used for web and business services: users and access, updates, firewalls, and a baseline configuration that reduces the obvious ways a host gets abused, then keep that baseline maintainable.

cards.name: Incident Response
cards.summary: Incident response for web and infrastructure issues: containment, investigation and a clear path back to a working service.
cards.what: I respond to incidents on systems I operate or have been asked to look after: contain the issue, investigate what happened, restore a working service, and write down the steps so the same failure is less likely to repeat.

cards.name: Disaster Recovery
cards.summary: Disaster recovery planning and restore rehearsals for servers, mail and web services, including backups you can actually use.
cards.what: I plan disaster recovery for servers, mail and web services: backups with retention you can restore from, a written restore path, and rehearsals so recovery is not a theory when a host or site fails.

cards.name: Cloudflare
cards.summary: Workers, Pages and DNS as supporting infrastructure tools.
cards.what: I use Cloudflare Workers, Pages and DNS when they are the right supporting tools for a deployment — alongside self-hosted Linux and Windows infrastructure, not in place of core engineering.

cards.name: Cloudflare Proxying
cards.summary: DNS routing, proxying, TLS, and edge caching.
cards.what: I configure DNS routing, proxying, TLS and edge caching so sites are reachable and cached at the edge. This is supporting infrastructure work, not a headline skill.

cards.name: Cloudflare Tunnels & Zero Trust
cards.summary: Cloudflare Tunnels and Zero Trust to publish and protect internal services without opening inbound ports.
cards.what: I set up Cloudflare Tunnels and Zero Trust access so internal services can be reached safely without opening inbound ports on the origin, including access policies for the people who need those services.

cards.name: Azure
cards.summary: Microsoft Azure as a supporting cloud for compute, storage and networking.
cards.what: I work with Azure when a project already lives there or needs Microsoft cloud services, as a supporting platform next to self-hosted infrastructure.

cards.name: AWS
cards.summary: Amazon Web Services as a supporting cloud for compute, storage and networking.
cards.what: I work with AWS when a project requires it, using it as a supporting cloud platform rather than the centre of how I design software and systems.

cards.name: Google Cloud
cards.summary: Google Cloud as a supporting platform for compute, storage, networking and developer services.
cards.what: I work with Google Cloud when a project already lives there or needs Google cloud services, as a supporting platform next to self-hosted infrastructure.

groups.name: Protocols, Commerce & Crypto
groups.summary: Interfaces between systems, payments in everyday currencies, and on-chain settlement.

cards.name: RPC and JSON-RPC
cards.summary: Remote procedure interfaces, including JSON-RPC services and clients.
cards.what: I design and integrate RPC and JSON-RPC interfaces so applications can call remote procedures with clear, documented payloads.

cards.name: REST
cards.summary: HTTP APIs with predictable resources and error handling.
cards.what: I build and consume REST APIs with clear resource paths, status codes and JSON payloads, suited to web applications and integrations.

cards.name: WebSockets
cards.summary: Two-way connections for live updates in the browser or between services.
cards.what: I use WebSockets when a product needs live updates — dashboards, messaging or operational views — with reconnection and error handling thought through.

cards.name: MQTT
cards.summary: Lightweight publish and subscribe messaging for devices and services.
cards.what: I integrate MQTT for publish-and-subscribe messaging between services or devices, including topics, quality of service and retained messages where they are needed.

cards.name: Webhooks
cards.summary: Signed HTTP callbacks for events between systems.
cards.what: I implement webhook senders and receivers with signature checks, retries and idempotent handling so event-driven integrations stay reliable.

cards.name: Modular plugins
cards.summary: Extension points so features can be added without rewriting the core.
cards.what: I design modular plugin hooks so a product can gain features later without a rewrite of the core, with a clear contract for each extension.

cards.name: Multi-currency fiat checkout and subscriptions
cards.summary: Card and wallet checkout, including subscriptions, in everyday currencies.
cards.what: I implement checkout and subscription flows for payments in everyday currencies, including receipts and the operational pages a buyer needs after paying.

cards.name: Stripe
cards.summary: Stripe checkout, subscriptions and payment webhooks for digital products and web platforms.
cards.what: I implement Stripe checkout and subscription flows, including webhooks, receipts and the operational pages a buyer needs after paying.

cards.name: PayPal
cards.summary: PayPal checkout for digital products, including receipts and post-purchase delivery.
cards.what: I implement PayPal checkout on product pages, with receipts from PayPal and delivery details sent to the email used at checkout.

cards.name: Square
cards.summary: Square checkout and payments for in-person and online sales, including receipts and settlements.
cards.what: I implement Square payments for in-person and online sales, including checkout, receipts and the settlement flow a small organisation needs after a payment is taken.

cards.name: Shopify
cards.summary: Shopify storefronts, themes, custom apps, checkout flows, and store integrations.
cards.what: I work on Shopify storefronts, themes, custom apps, checkout flows and store integrations, including the surrounding webhooks and payment work.

cards.name: WooCommerce
cards.summary: WooCommerce storefronts on WordPress, including catalogue, checkout and payment integrations.
cards.what: I build and maintain WooCommerce storefronts on WordPress: catalogue, checkout, payment integrations and the surrounding pages a buyer needs after paying.

cards.name: Storefront
cards.summary: Storefronts for digital products and retail, including Shopify and custom checkout pages.
cards.what: I build and adapt storefronts for digital products and retail, including Shopify storefronts and custom product pages with PayPal or Stripe checkout and email delivery.

cards.name: Social Media Marketing
cards.summary: Social media marketing for a professional practice: public profiles, consistent messaging, and links back to the site.
cards.what: I plan and keep social media marketing for a professional practice: a public profile, consistent messaging, and links back to the site so enquiries land on hire or contact pages rather than in a closed inbox alone.

cards.name: Cryptocurrency wallets
cards.summary: Wallet flows for holding and sending supported digital assets.
cards.what: I build wallet-related application flows — send, receive and balance views — with careful handling of keys and confirmation, for products that need them.

cards.name: RPC nodes
cards.summary: Connections to blockchain RPC nodes for reads and transaction broadcast.
cards.what: I connect applications to blockchain RPC nodes for reads and transaction broadcast, with clear handling of node errors, fees and confirmation.

cards.name: On-chain settlement
cards.summary: Recording and confirming value transfer on a supported chain.
cards.what: I implement on-chain settlement in applications that need it: constructing transfers, waiting for confirmation, and recording the result against an order or account.
